_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
EVERY FIELD HAS A WORD CAP, and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build past it:
name 16, why 40, risk 80, touches 80, note 120, comment 120, askedBy.detail 80. A
session with more to say than that puts it in the feature's Brief or history file
and links it. ONE FACT, ONE HOME: replace a sentence that is out of date; never append
an UPDATED paragraph beneath it. On 2026-09-03 one item's comment had grown to 1,388
words across seven sessions that way, and Mike could not read his own list.
activeOn: { machine, since } says which computer is working an item right now —
'laptop' or 'desktop', from the date given. Mike's instruction, 2026-09-03, after item
4.54 was built on both machines in the same week. Absent means nobody is on it. The
page shows it as a column, the control shows it on the row, and the control's save
carries it through. Shutdown clears or keeps it; startup reports the other machine's.
rankedByMike: false marks an item filed after orderedByMikeOn that Mike has not yet
placed. The page and the Handbook control show it. It clears itself: the control's
export does not carry the field, so his next saved list drops it.
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.

items.name: Depreciation rates per country - a manager uploads the source, the AI proposes, they approve
items.why: Depreciation rates and first-year rules differ by country and nothing in the app holds them. The shipped defaults are a guess: Vehicles is 20% where NZ IRD gives 50% diminishing value for a passenger vehicle.
items.risk: An advisor who leaves a default produces a forecast whose depreciation, tax and closing cash are all wrong, and which balances perfectly, and it reaches a lender. The counter-risk is the AI misreading a rate nobody re-checks - which is why the manager approves the extracted table before anything reads it, and why every figure carries its source document and date.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-08 - 'is it worth having a field in the firm manager hub where tax pdfs can be loaded to be read by the AI so it can be accurate per country?' Filed on his yes, after he overturned the recommendation against it: the uploader is an accountant who should be encouraged to check their sources.

items.touches: A new Firm Manager Hub tab and its upload route, the untrusted-file validation procedure in the master-export-upload skill (last-known-good, version history), an OpenAI extraction route on the Restify backend, an approval gate carrying isApproved, and the six ASSET_SPECS defaults in components/ThreeWayForecastIntake.vue that it would replace.
items.note: NOTHING READS AN UNAPPROVED TABLE, structurally rather than by a flag: a proposal lives in its own store. THE MANAGER'S SIDE IS COMPLETE, slices 1 to 3b. SLICES 4 AND 5 ARE THE ADVISOR'S HALF: each rate badges its origin; an approved table is OFFERED, filling only rates still on defaults so a typed rate survives; and an advisor may LOAD a document while approval stays manager-only. ⚠ THE AI-CALL EXPOSURE THAT WIDENING CREATED IS ITEM 4.82, not a warning here. NOT BUILT: the dated purchase list with the first-year deduction - item 4.77, closed here. No document has been read in earnest; that needs UAT. Detail is in the Brief; rulings in depreciation-rates-history.md.

Spec Kit produced eleven rulings, Investment Boost among them. Slices 4 and 5 built the same day on his yes: the advisor sees where each rate came from, is offered their country's table, and may load a document their manager decides on. 44 new tests.

items.name: The forecast's tax rates are New Zealand's, hardcoded, for every country
items.why: The forecast applies New Zealand's company tax rate, GST rate and filing cycle to every client in every country, with nothing on screen saying so and no manager able to change it.
items.risk: Every forecast for an overseas client is wrong on tax whether or not it owns a single asset, so this is WIDER than 4.78. An advisor can type over the two rates but is never told they are New Zealand's; the filing cycle they cannot change at all, and it decides which months the money leaves the bank. The statements balance perfectly, which is how it reaches a lender.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-08 - 'is it worth having a field in the firm manager hub where tax pdfs can be loaded to be read by the AI so it can be accurate per country?' The same request 4.78 was filed under.

items.touches: server/utils/taxRates.js and sourcedFigure.js, server/routes/taxRates.js, the Tax Rates tab in components/firm/FirmTaxRates.vue at all four tiers, the GST filing cycle in server/report/threeWayForecastModel.js, and the country field and tax card in components/ThreeWayForecastIntake.vue.
items.note: BUILT, SLICES 1-5, AND A SEPARATE TAB FROM DEPRECIATION RATES ON MIKE'S APPROVAL: the country table, the cascade, the routes, the manager's screen, the engine and the advisor's side. FOUR FIGURES, NOT TWO - the drawing found the GST section also fixes the filing cycle and the accounting basis, both New Zealand's. THE ENGINE'S THREE HARDCODED CYCLES BECAME ONE FORMULA, so Australia's quarterly BAS can be expressed at all; the 3,385 golden workbook cells pass unchanged. NOT BUILT: loading a tax PDF for the AI to read, drawn in §4 - today a manager types each figure and its source by hand. Company tax stays ONE flat rate with a free-text line naming which entities it reaches.
items.comment: 2026-09-09 - Mike's own words when the gap was reported as something he had not asked for: 'of course i want the tax rate made contry aware - i literally asked for that!' He had. Drawing approved the same day, then built in five slices on the laptop. The item's own wording was corrected in the build: both rates WERE already editable by an advisor, so the fault was never 'nothing can change them' but 'they are silently New Zealand's and no manager can set them'. The country field was built here on his explicit yes - it is 4.78's approved addendum and nothing here resolves without it.

items.name: Nothing caps how many paid AI readings an advisor can trigger
items.why: Loading a tax document sends it to the model and every reading is paid for. Nothing caps how many one person may set off, and the store's 20-document limit trims only after the model has already been paid.
items.risk: An advisor inside a real firm could load the same PDF over and over and run up a bill nobody sees until it arrives. No data leaks and no wrong figure reaches a client, which is why this is a 2 and not a 5. It is not new in kind - a manager could always do it - but 2026-09-09 widened it from managers to every advisor.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-09-09 while building 4.78 slice 5, the change that widened it, and raised with Mike the same day. Filed at his instruction rather than left as a warning inside 4.78's note.

items.touches: server/restify-server.js, where the advisor's load route and the manager's sit beside each other, and server/routes/depreciationRates.js loadDocument, which both reach and which calls the model. A cap belongs there, never on the screen - a screen-side limit is not a limit.
items.note: NO CAP EXISTS ANYWHERE TODAY, on the advisor's route or the manager's. The store's 20-document limit is not one: it trims AFTER the model has been paid. Mike's ruling of 2026-09-08 that an advisor may load is NOT in question here - only whether the loading is capped, and at what. A first cap could be per firm per day, which needs nothing this app does not already know.
items.comment: 2026-09-09 - filed at shutdown on Mike's yes, having first been written as a warning inside 4.78's note. That is the shape this list explicitly refuses: a hazard nobody owns gets described repeatedly and fixed never. Scored 2 rather than 5 deliberately - no data leaks, no wrong figure reaches a client, and it takes an authenticated advisor inside a real firm to spend anything.
